question.problem:
Find the smallest natural number solution to the system of linear congruences below.

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x≡0 & (\text{mod}\,2) \\ x≡4 & (\text{mod}\,5) \\ x≡7 & (\text{mod}\,9)\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
Since $2,$ $5,$ and $9$ are coprime, then according to the Chinese remainder theorem, the system has a unique solution modulo $2\cdot 5\cdot 9=90.$

We will solve the system in two steps.

**Step 1.** Find the common solution for the first and second congruences of the system.

From the first congruence, we get

$$
x≡0\,(\text{mod}\,2)\,⟹\,x=2t,\,t\in Z.
$$

Substituting this into the second congruence, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ≡4 &  & \,(\text{mod}\,5) \\ 2t & ≡4 &  & \,(\text{mod}\,5) \\ t & ≡2 &  & \,(\text{mod}\,5)\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, $t=2+5s,$ where $s\in Z.$ Substituting this into the expression for $x,$ we get the common solution for the first and second congruences:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =2t \\  & =2(2+5s) \\  & =4+10s\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 2.** Find the common solution of all three congruences.

Now, substituting the common solution of the first two congruences into the third congruence, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ≡7 &  & \,(\text{mod}\,9) \\ 4+10s & ≡7 &  & \,(\text{mod}\,9) \\ 10s & ≡3 &  & \,(\text{mod}\,9) \\ s & ≡3 &  & \,(\text{mod}\,9)\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, $s=3+9u,$ where $u\in Z.$ Substituting this into the expression for the common solution of the first two congruences, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =4+10s \\  & =4+10(3+9u) \\  & =34+90u.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $x≡34\,(\text{mod}\,90)$ is the unique solution modulo $90,$ and $x=34$ is the smallest natural number solution to the system.
